editorialNotes: The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy 2024 revision and Joseph A. Adler’s academic survey were read. They support the existing treatment of education, official service, travels and posthumous transmission.
551–479 BCE remains a traditional chronology, not a modern archival verification. Offices and travels are attributed to transmitted accounts; no exact month or day is invented.
The Analects is a compilation transmitted by later followers. Competing accounts and modern excavated textual evidence do not justify presenting later transmission as a new event in Confucius’s life.
Ancient biographical evidence cannot satisfy a modern archival standard; this limitation is retained explicitly. No new life event was identified.
This is an AI editorial and translation review; no human or native-speaker certification is asserted.
The existing stable item IDs, life status and rating fields are preserved. No influence rating is added. The chronology is selective, not a complete daily record.
